ON THE 18 th OF AUGUST, 2023  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 29029 of 2023  BETWEEN:-
 BHOLA @ ANMOL S/O SHRI TEKSINGH GOND, AGED  ABOUT 21 YEARS, OCCUPATION: LABOUR, R/O  JOGIKHEDA, P.S. JABERA, DISTRICT- DAMOH  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI ASHISH TIWARI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  1. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH  POLICE STATION PATERA, DISTRICT- DAMOH  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 2. VICTIM A D/O NOT MENTION NOT MENTION  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 .
 (BY SMT. RANJANA AGNIHOTRI - DY. GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
This application coming on for admission this day,

This is first application filed by applicant under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail to applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.42/2023, dated 15.02.2023 registered at Police Station Patera, District Damoh for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Sections 3/4 and 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody and trial will take considerable time to be concluded.
The applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

The applicant is a permanent resident of district and is ready to furnish adequate surety and Bhola @ Anmol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121620009/
1 shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
In the FIR, it is claimed that the prosecutrix was around 15 years at the time of the incident as she had not studied in any school.
Her ossification test was done for age determination in which her age is estimated between 17-18 years.
Her statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. have been perused.

In the light of her statements and looking to the age of the prosecutrix, this Court finds it fit to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Bhola @ Anmol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121620009/
